title: Kratie Travel Guide: Mekong, Koh Trong & Dolphins | roammate
description: Spend three days in Kratie with Koh Trong, the Mekong riverfront and responsible dolphin watching at Kampi, plus practical transport and budget planning.
heroSubtitle: Slow down beside the Mekong: island lanes, market breakfasts and a thoughtful approach to watching Cambodia's river dolphins.

3.title: Get to know the Mekong town

periods.title: Breakfast and the central market
periods.text: Begin with a short walk around Kratie's central market and surrounding streets rather than heading straight out on a tour. Find breakfast being cooked to order, ask before photographing stallholders and notice how everyday trading connects the town to the river. Keep purchases small enough to carry comfortably. This is a useful morning for finding drinking water, checking transport offices and getting a feel for your accommodation's neighbourhood without committing to a long outing in the heat.
periods.tip: This plan assumes three full days after arrival. If your journey into Kratie consumes the morning, move the market walk to the next available breakfast rather than rushing it.

periods.title: Plan the river days properly
periods.text: Use a shaded lunch break to arrange the next two days. For Koh Trong, ask where the passenger boat is boarding now, what the return arrangements are and whether bicycles are available on the island. For Kampi, compare a road transfer plus locally arranged viewing boat with a guided kayaking option appropriate to your experience. Ask about river conditions and cancellation procedures before paying. Keep the two excursions on separate days so you can move one if weather changes.
periods.tip: Get the complete cost in writing: road transport, boat or kayak, guide, equipment, waiting time and return transfer. A low advertised activity price may omit the journey from town.

periods.title: Riverfront light and a local dinner
periods.text: Head to the Mekong-facing riverfront as the day cools. Sit somewhere that leaves the walking route clear and enjoy the changing light; a colourful sunset is a possibility, not an appointment. For dinner, ask about Khmer dishes available that evening. Kratie's regional food includes bamboo-cooked sticky rice and pomelos from Koh Trong, worth looking for during your stay when available. Finish early enough to prepare water, sun protection and a small day bag for the island.
periods.tip: Choose a busy place that can explain ingredients. Vegetarian-looking dishes may still contain fish sauce, shrimp paste or meat stock.

periods.title: Cross to Koh Trong
periods.text: Take the confirmed passenger crossing to Koh Trong, the Mekong island opposite town, when the operator considers conditions suitable. Wear a correctly fitting lifejacket and keep valuables dry. On arrival, choose a bicycle or a modest walk according to the heat and the route surface. Ask about the public route rather than cutting through orchards or household yards. Keep the morning focused on the island itself: the pleasure is in travelling slowly, not in collecting stops before another excursion.
periods.tip: Check the practical boarding situation on both banks. A boat crossing can involve sand, slippery slopes and carrying bags even when the water journey is short.

periods.title: A hosted lunch and a shorter loop
periods.text: Arrange lunch with a willing local business or host, confirming the meal and price in advance. Ask about pomelo growing or daily island life without treating someone's work as a free demonstration. Continue only as far as feels comfortable, taking shade breaks and turning back if the route is muddy or waterlogged. If you want to stay overnight, book a host and meals first; otherwise return to the landing with ample time before your agreed crossing back to Kratie.
periods.tip: Do not use a claimed last-boat time from an old article. Reconfirm the return with the boat operator on the day and keep their contact details.

periods.title: Back in town, with tomorrow flexible
periods.text: After the island, return to your accommodation for a shower and an unhurried dinner. Reconfirm the Kampi outing, especially after heavy rain or a change in river conditions. If water activities have been cancelled, choose a town-based day rather than searching for someone willing to ignore the same conditions. An extra café stop, market visit or riverside walk is a reasonable part of a small-town stay, not a failure to complete the itinerary.
periods.tip: Keep some dry cash and a charged phone separate from the bag used on the boat. Do not leave all your money or travel documents in a handlebar basket.

periods.title: Choose a careful wildlife outing
periods.text: Travel to the Kampi dolphin-viewing area north of Kratie with a prearranged return. Listen to the boat crew's briefing and ask them to follow the current local viewing rules. Stay seated, keep noise low and accept distant or brief views. Do not encourage a chase, a closer approach for a photograph or extra time around animals that are moving away. A guided kayak trip can be an alternative, not an automatic guarantee of lower impact or suitability for beginners.
periods.tip: No operator can guarantee a wild dolphin sighting. Take binoculars if you have them, and judge the excursion by how the crew behaves, not how close the animals come.

periods.title: Return slowly, or add one land stop
periods.text: Leave the rest of the day open after the water outing. If you chose a longer guided paddle, lunch and the return journey may be enough. With a shorter boat trip and a willing driver, ask whether Sambok Hill is an appropriate extra stop on the way back, checking access and your energy for steps before agreeing. Do not add a distant temple circuit simply because it appears on the same provincial map. Head back to Kratie before you are exhausted.
periods.tip: Choose the hill only if local conditions and your mobility allow. Comfortable shoes, modest clothing and water matter more than fitting in an additional photograph.

periods.title: One final Mekong evening
periods.text: Spend your final evening in town, settle outstanding transport arrangements and enjoy dinner without a long drive afterwards. If you did not see dolphins, resist turning the next morning into a rushed repeat before a bus connection. Kratie also offers the island, food and river landscape you have already experienced. Keep onward travel separate from this full-day plan, particularly if you are continuing towards Stung Treng or crossing into another country.
periods.tip: Check tomorrow's actual departure point rather than assuming every service leaves from the same station. Keep a buffer before any flight or international connection.

budgetIntro: Editorial planning estimates in US dollars, prepared September 2026, not live prices or quoted tariffs. Amounts are per person per day; midrange accommodation assumes two sharing. Transport and activity rows are averages across three days, not a dolphin-tour price list. Excludes travel to/from Kratie, visas, insurance, alcohol and premium private excursions. Solo transport or a guided kayaking day can exceed the daily average.

budgetTips.title: Price the Kampi day as a whole
budgetTips.text: Ask for road transfer, boat arrangements, guide, waiting time and return travel in one breakdown. Clarify whether each charge is per person or per vehicle before comparing options.

budgetTips.title: Stay in town for simpler logistics
budgetTips.text: A central room can reduce transport to dinner and departure offices. An island stay is a different experience, but add crossings, luggage handling and meal arrangements before comparing the room price.

budgetTips.title: Share transparently, not at the wildlife's expense
budgetTips.text: Sharing a suitable vehicle with other travellers can lower the cost. Do not overload a boat or choose an operator promising close encounters simply because the fare is lower.

budgetTips.title: Keep a low-cost day in the plan
budgetTips.text: The town and island days provide a counterweight to a paid guided excursion. Leave space for walking and rest rather than booking three consecutive tours.

practicalInfo.title: Getting to Kratie and continuing onward
items: Plan a road journey rather than assuming Kratie has a scheduled passenger-air or rail connection. Check dated bus or minivan departures from Phnom Penh with the operator. Vireak Buntham is one booking reference; confirm Kratie as the actual destination, not an intermediate roadside drop.

From Siem Reap or towards Stung Treng, ask whether the service is direct, where any vehicle change occurs and which luggage is included. No fixed frequency, journey duration or through-ticket connection is promised here. Use the operator's current booking page and a separate transfer buffer.

For onward Laos travel, verify the exact border crossing, nationality-specific visa rules and current operating status independently. A ticket seller's offer does not establish immigration eligibility. Do not assume an e-Visa works at every land crossing.

practicalInfo.title: Dolphin watching and river safety
items: Kampi is a recognised dolphin-viewing destination. WWF describes the wider Kratie–Stung Treng river area as important dolphin habitat. Population estimates change and are not a probability of seeing animals on a particular trip; this guide does not promise sightings or publish a stale dolphin count.

Ask about current local approach rules and how the crew avoids disturbing animals. Prefer patient observation, no chasing and space for animals to move away. Do not feed, touch or swim with dolphins. These are editorial wildlife-welfare recommendations informed by the IWC handbook, not a claim that every operator is certified or that one international distance rule applies locally.

Check correctly fitting lifejackets, boat condition, guide communication and cancellation procedures. Wear the lifejacket rather than leaving it on the floor. Kayaking requires a briefing appropriate to the route, current and your ability; do not assume calm-looking water is safe for unsupervised swimming or paddling.

practicalInfo.title: Koh Trong practicalities
items: Confirm the passenger landing and return arrangements locally on the day. Water level can affect the approach to the boat. Carry only what you can manage on uneven ground and ask for details if you have limited mobility.

Arrange bicycle rental, a meal or an overnight stay with a willing provider instead of assuming every household takes visitors. Inspect brakes and tyres, carry water and use public routes. Ask before entering orchards, homes or religious spaces.

CRDT documents waste-management work on Koh Trong. Help by reducing disposable packaging and asking where sorted rubbish belongs; do not leave litter on the riverbank or assume an island business can process everything brought over by visitors.

practicalInfo.title: When to go
items: Cambodia's national climate report describes a generally dry November–April and wet May–October, with hotter weather towards April and early May. November–January is a sensible starting point for travellers seeking less heat. These are broad seasonal patterns, not a forecast for your dates.

Schedule exposed walking and cycling earlier, leave a shaded midday break and carry drinking water. In wetter months, ask about river conditions and flood-affected roads before confirming island or boat excursions. Keep the order of days flexible and postpone water activities during unsafe weather.

practicalInfo.title: Travel advice, health and entry
items: Checked 12 September 2026: UK FCDO advice warns against all but essential travel within 20km of Cambodia's land border with Thailand and says Cambodia–Thailand land crossings remain suspended. This is a geographically specific warning, not a blanket restriction on Kratie. Check the full current advice for every part of your route and your insurer's conditions.

Use established roads and paths, secure belongings and arrange reliable evening transport. Check FCDO safety and health guidance before travel; seek personalised travel-health advice and insurance covering your chosen activities. This itinerary is not a safety guarantee.

Consult the official Cambodia e-Visa portal and current entry guidance for the passport, visa and arrival requirements relevant to your nationality and entry point. Keep a copy of your documents separately, and do not hand over your passport as casual rental security.

practicalInfo.title: Accommodation, cash and connectivity
items: For easy first-visit logistics, search around the central market and Mekong riverfront, then read recent reviews for noise, air-conditioning and access. A Koh Trong overnight needs more advance coordination and does not suit every early departure.

Carry small cash for boats, markets and short rides. Confirm whether a bill is in riel or US dollars and agree the conversion before paying. Foreign cards and local QR systems should not be your only payment options.

Save offline maps, your accommodation address in Khmer and driver/operator contacts. Carry a charged phone and dry protection for electronics. Tell your host where you are going when heading out on the river.

culturalIntro: A river village, an island household and a dolphin habitat are not interchangeable tourist stops. Let residents and wildlife determine the boundaries of your visit.

culturalTips.title: Make island visits an invitation
culturalTips.text: Public lanes are not permission to enter yards or photograph family life. Ask before taking portraits, accept a refusal and agree payment for a hosted meal or activity in advance.

culturalTips.title: Treat temples as active religious places
culturalTips.text: Cover shoulders and knees, follow instructions about shoes and photography, and keep clear of worshippers. Skip steps that exceed your ability instead of taking a shortcut through restricted ground.

culturalTips.title: Do not reward a closer chase
culturalTips.text: If an animal moves away, let the encounter end. Ask your guide about conservation rather than asking for a better selfie. A patient outing with distant views is preferable to pressuring wildlife.

culturalTips.title: Pay for produce and time
culturalTips.text: Ask growers or sellers which fruit is available and what it costs. Do not pick pomelos or enter orchards without permission, even if a path runs beside them.

culturalTips.title: Reduce what you bring onto the island
culturalTips.text: Take a reusable bottle and bag, ask about safe refill water and keep wrappers out of the Mekong. Respect local waste-separation arrangements rather than leaving everything in the first bin.

culturalTips.title: Support work, not staged access
culturalTips.text: Choose clearly explained services and businesses that welcome visitors. Do not distribute gifts to children or treat schools and homes as attractions without an appropriate invitation.

ctaText: Planning a slower Mekong stop? Use roammate to look for travel companions interested in island cycling, local food and a carefully arranged shared excursion.
ctaCustomise: Adapt this plan to your dates, river conditions and confirmed transport, leaving enough time to enjoy Kratie without rushing the wildlife.
